io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.core.services.localization

Class ItemTranslationService

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.core.services.localization.ItemTranslationService

  • public class ItemTranslationService
extends java.lang.Object
    Translates Slimefun item names and lore per language. Translations live in languages/<lang>/items.yml (keyed by item id -> name + lore), shipped by core and by addons. The current hardcoded names remain the built-in English fallback, so a missing translation simply shows English. Used by the Guide and other Slimefun UIs to display items in the viewing player's language; the coverage map powers the per-plugin translation percentage in the UI.

      • registerTranslations

        public void registerTranslations(@Nonnull
                                 org.bukkit.plugin.java.JavaPlugin addon)
        Lets an addon contribute its own languages/<lang>/items.yml translations. Call this from the addon's onEnable after its items are registered. The addon's items are then also canonicalized to their id-name (the packet layer renders the per-viewer translated display).

      • canonicalizeToId

        public void canonicalizeToId()
        Bakes every registered item's template to id-only: display name = the raw id, no lore. No baked text may ever show on a surface the packet layer does not reach (dropped items, item frames, entity equipment, villager trades, unsupported server versions, or translation.packets=false) - the packet layer is the only place a translated/composed display is produced, per viewer, at send time.

      • registerResolver

        public void registerResolver(@Nonnull
                             ItemTextResolver resolver)
        Registers a dynamic ItemTextResolver for runtime-generated items. Consulted only for ids with no explicit items.yml entry or %MOB% family, ahead of the english/raw-id fallback. Drops the render cache so any id previously shown as a raw-id re-renders through it.

      • renderForPacket

        public ItemTranslationService.RenderedDisplay renderForPacket(@Nonnull
                                                              java.lang.String id,
                                                              @Nullable
                                                              java.lang.String languageId,
                                                              @Nonnull
                                                              TranslationConfig.FallbackMode fallback,
                                                              boolean includeDescription)
        Renders an item's per-viewer display (name + composed lore) for the given language. Pure and thread-safe: reads only the loaded translation data (populated once at boot, read-only afterward) plus the thread-safe render cache, so it is safe to call from the Netty thread. Returns null only when nothing at all is known about the id - neither a registered item nor an items.yml entry - which is the caller's signal to humanize the raw id.

        The viewer's language is resolved ONCE, up front, into a single effective language: the given languageId if non-null, otherwise the server's default language id (or null if there is no default language). That single effective language is then used for BOTH the name lookup and the lore blocks, so the two can never resolve against different languages. Only once that lookup comes back empty does the fallback mode decide the missing label (the raw id, or the English baseline name/lore).

        Parameters:
        id - the Slimefun item id
        languageId - the viewer's language id, or null to use the server's default language
        fallback - what a missing label becomes (ENGLISH or ID)

      • renderForPacketWithItem

        public ItemTranslationService.RenderedDisplay renderForPacketWithItem(@Nonnull
                                                                      org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack item,

        Packet-path render that has the actual ItemStack. Tries per-instance ItemTextResolvers first (passing the stack, e.g. for SlimeTinker tools whose name depends on their PDC parts); those results are NOT cached since they vary per stack. Falls back to renderForPacket(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.core.services.localization.TranslationConfig.FallbackMode, boolean) (which handles static entries, id-keyed resolvers and the english/raw fallback, and caches).

      • wasAuthorEnchantHidden

        public boolean wasAuthorEnchantHidden(@Nonnull
                                      java.lang.String id)
        Whether the item's author marked its enchantment(s) hidden (ItemFlag.HIDE_ENCHANTS) on the original, pre-bake template - the standard "glow only" trick, where a meaningless enchant is added purely for the enchanted glint. Read from the English baseline (captured before our own bake adds HIDE_ENCHANTS to re-render enchants) so the re-render pass never mistakes its own flag for the author's intent. EnchantDisplay keeps such enchants hidden (no lore line), leaving only the glint.

      • auditUnmigratedLore

        public void auditUnmigratedLore(@Nonnull
                                java.io.File out)
        Boot audit of translation coverage: for every enabled item (except VanillaItem), flags two independent gaps and writes the full per-addon breakdown to out. Runs each launch so the migration to the unified name/lore system stays visible.
        • untranslated-name - no explicit name: entry in any language's items.yml (and not deliberately English-everywhere via FallbackSafe). Such an item shows its hardcoded English name, or - if it has none - the raw vanilla/id name to every viewer. This is why e.g. SlimeTinker's assembled tools look untranslated even though the addon ships an items.yml: the registered id simply isn't a key in it.
        • hardcoded-lore - the template still carries hardcoded lore and has no type/description/stats/usage block, so its lore can't be localized.
        Both checks are family-aware (an id resolved from a %MOB% template counts as covered), so runtime-generated item families are not false-positived.

      • getItemUnitCoverage

        @Nonnull
public java.util.Map<java.lang.String,int[]> getItemUnitCoverage(@Nonnull
                                                                          java.lang.String language)
        Leaf-based coverage of a language per plugin: pluginName -> [coveredUnits, totalUnits], over all enabled items grouped by their addon. A unit is one of an item's translatable leaves: name (if English has one) plus each of type/description/stats/usage that English defines non-empty. This counts real block coverage (not mere entry presence), so a language with translated names but untranslated lore blocks scores well below 100%. An item id tagged in FallbackSafe.itemIds() counts every one of its English units as covered (deliberately English-everywhere). Items with zero English units contribute nothing (they can't inflate or deflate the percentage). Powers the translation-percentage UI.
